findings.title: Make the laser occlusion test reach the line-of-sight check
findings.claim: The purported blocked-laser case passes because the target is out of range, so it does not exercise laser occlusion.
findings.evidence: tests/tacticalWeapons.test.ts:72 places ships 600 units apart. src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/weapons.ts:41 rejects distances above 450 before evaluating lineOfSight at L42. Removing that lineOfSight call in memory left all 52 test bodies passing under the Node assertion harness. Spec L140 requires occlusion.
findings.why: The geometry tests verify the helper, but cannot detect the laser firing through obstacles because its caller stops using that helper.
findings.fix: Use an in-range, in-arc blocked fixture, such as ships at (-200, 0) and (200, 0), and release a full charge. Assert a miss and unchanged target damage; include an asteroid-blocked case.

findings.title: Test shield-clock preservation with nonzero progress
findings.claim: The level-2 shield test freezes an already-zero clock and never checks repair resumption, so resetting instead of preserving progress passes.
findings.evidence: tests/tacticalWeapons.test.ts:118 reaches two layers, then L119 disables recharge without giving the clock nonzero progress; L121 consequently captures zero. src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/weapons.ts:86-L87 implements the behavior required by spec L101. An in-memory mutation resetting shieldClock whenever Shields is level 2 left all 52 test bodies passing.
findings.why: Losing accumulated recharge during damage or repair violates an explicit state-preservation rule and would escape the current regression tests.
findings.fix: Accumulate nonzero recharge before setting Shields to level 2, assert that exact value throughout the freeze, then repair to level 1 and verify resumed increments and the exact layer-completion tick.

findings.title: Exercise the hunter's temporal and RNG invariants
findings.claim: The hunter tests do not establish their claimed lead time, 18-tick history delay, or single jitter draw.
findings.evidence: tests/tacticalHunter.test.ts:12-L13 gives the lead test stationary ships; L93 fills every trail entry identically; L61 checks only that RNG changed. The relevant implementation is src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/hunter.ts:58-L59, L69 and L82. Independently removing the velocity lead, reading the newest trail slot, or adding an extra nextInt draw left all 52 test bodies passing in the in-memory harness. Spec L201-L202 requires all three invariants.
findings.why: These regressions change pursuit behavior and the deterministic RNG sequence while preserving every current assertion.
findings.fix: Use a moving target whose lead changes the expected steering; feed distinguishable positions through multiple ring-buffer wraps and assert the exact 18-tick delay; compare RNG state against exactly one nextInt call and assert no further draws while a release remains scheduled. Cover cancellation and rescheduling.
